# Hermes Agent FAQ & Troubleshooting Guide

## 1. General Architecture & Web UI
- **Is there a Web UI?** Yes. Run `hermes dashboard` to launch the local web interface on `http://127.0.0.1:9119`, which includes an embedded browser chat.
- **Observability / Tracing:** Langfuse is bundled as an opt-in plugin. Enable via `hermes tools` or `hermes plugins enable observability/langfuse` to view full turn execution traces and tool input/output parameter chains.
- **Reporting Vulnerabilities:** Follow `SECURITY.md` guidelines: report via [GitHub Security Advisories](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/security/advisories/new) or email `security@nousresearch.com`.

---

## 2. Model Providers & Authentication
- **Local Ollama Overridden by Env Keys:** If you configure local models (e.g., `base_url: http://localhost:11434`) and Hermes hits remote endpoints with 401 errors (like Anthropic), set `provider: custom` in `~/.hermes/config.yaml` instead of `provider: auto`.
- **Ollama Cloud 404 Errors:** Ollama Cloud uses OpenAI-compatible `/v1` routes (`https://ollama.com/v1`). Select the built-in `ollama-cloud` provider.
- **Small Local Models (4B–9B) Are Slow:** The agent passes the full tool schema (~45 tools) on each turn. Speed it up by:
  1. Disabling unused toolsets via `hermes tools`.
  2. Using quantized builds.
  3. Setting `terminal.backend: local` to remove container overhead.
- **Ollama / Custom Vision:** Set `supports_vision: true` under your custom model configuration to pass native image payloads.
- **Azure AI Foundry:** Run `hermes setup` or set `provider: azure-foundry`. It auto-detects `ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_BASE_URL`. Claude Code env vars like `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY` are ignored.
- **Claude Pro/Max vs. API Mode:** Using an Anthropic API key always incurs standard API billing. To use subscription allowances, authenticate via OAuth.
- **Google Gemini OAuth:** `google-gemini-cli` OAuth was removed due to upstream policy bans. Use Google AI Studio with `GOOGLE_API_KEY` or `GEMINI_API_KEY`.
- **DeepSeek V4 Routing:** If `deepseek-v4-flash` runs on `deepseek-chat` rates, upgrade Hermes to avoid legacy normalization aliases mapping to `deepseek-v4-pro`.
- **LocalAI Token Usage:** OpenAI-compatible streaming automatically forwards `stream_options: {include_usage: true}` for token tracking in `/usage`.

---

## 3. Policy & Extensibility
- **Smart / Dynamic Model Routing:** Deprecated and not supported. The session model is strictly maintained. To configure subagents, use `delegation.provider` / `delegation.model` in `config.yaml` or change manually with `/model`.
- **Custom Memory Backends:** In-tree additions to `plugins/memory/` are closed. Third-party providers (e.g., YantrikDB) must be installed as standalone plugins under `~/.hermes/plugins/` implementing the `MemoryProvider` ABC (`sync_turn`, `prefetch`, `shutdown`).
- **Custom Tools:** Custom tools should be packaged as plugins in `~/.hermes/plugins` and enabled via `hermes plugins enable <name>`. Core development requires definitions in `tools/` and registry in `toolsets.py`.

---

## 4. Agent Loops, Persona & Context
- **Tool Limits & Long Autonomous Runs:** Standard limit is controlled by `agent.max_turns` (default: 90; CLI override: `hermes chat --max-turns <N>`). For persistent tasks across interruptions, use `/goal` (Ralph loop) and resume paused runs with `/goal resume`.
- **Context Compaction:** Old tool outputs are automatically pruned by `ContextCompressor`. Pluggable alternatives can be configured under `context.engine`.
- **Subagents & Delegation:** Spawn concurrent subagents (default up to 3) using `delegate_task`.
- **Agent Identity & Memory:** 
  - `SOUL.md`: Base agent persona/backstory.
  - `USER.md` (`target="user"`): Persistent user preferences and profile.
  - `MEMORY.md`: Agent knowledge and general facts.
  - Check skill execution statistics with `/insights` or `hermes insights` (tracks `~/.hermes/skills/.usage.json`).

---

## 5. Gateway & Messaging Integrations
- **Setup Wizard:** Configure Discord and other platforms interactively with `hermes gateway setup`.
- **Telegram "Unauthorized user" Fix:** `allowed_chats` only controls group IDs. For DM user access, add the numeric ID to `allow_from` (sets `TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USERS`), use pairing approval (`hermes pairing approve telegram <CODE>`), or enable `allow_all: true`.
- **Per-Channel Personas:** Define ephemeral personas per room/channel ID across Discord, Telegram, Slack, and Mattermost via `channel_prompts`.
- **Multiplexing Profiles:** Multiple user profiles/accounts (e.g., separate WeChat/Weixin or Telegram configs) can run under a single gateway instance while keeping credentials and memory isolated.
- **File Transfers:** Local output files and MCP tools returning image tags (`MEDIA:<path>`) are natively dispatched to Matrix (`m.file`), Telegram, and Email (SMTP attachments). DingTalk supports markdown images (`![image](url)`).
- **Inbound Attachments:** Uploaded text and code files (e.g., `.py`, `.txt`) are automatically injected into prompt context.
- **Session Continuity:** Sessions interrupted by gateway reboots persist in `resume_pending` state; auto-reset defaults to `mode: none`.

---

## 6. Installation & Platform Issues
- **Windows Support:** Windows 10/11 is a Tier 1 platform via `install.ps1` without requiring WSL2 (WSL2 remains recommended only if using the Dashboard POSIX PTY terminal).
- **Docker / NAS Permissions (`Permission denied`):** Map host user permissions using `PUID` and `PGID` (or `HERMES_UID`/`HERMES_GID`) to ensure container access to persistent volumes like `/opt/data`. Multi-arch Docker images natively support `linux/arm64` (Raspberry Pi, Apple Silicon).
- **Android / Termux:** Native support provided via `.[termux-all]` dependencies in `scripts/install.sh`.
- **Local Honcho Memory:** Local instances (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`) do not require API keys; the client auto-injects a placeholder credential.
- **Slow Updates:** Silent stalls during `hermes update` under Node.js are due to Camofox binary downloads.
